thread.title: Apple proves it can still deliver profit growth despite slower iPhone demand (AAPL)

author: jollyjetta
title: Apple proves it can still deliver profit growth despite slower iPhone demand (AAPL)
text: in General Apple reported an earnings beat despite weaker-than-expected iPhone sales.Some analysts believe that its strong services, revenue from other products, and potential for capital return helped offset iPhone numbers. Watch - Apple - Stock - Price - Time Watch Apple's stock price in real time here. Even though Apple sold fewer iPhones than it anticipated for the holiday quarter, the company blew past Wall Street estimates in its Q1 earnings report. And analysts noted that there were other factors at play besides the high cost of the new iPhone X that helped Apple's success. Company - Earnings - Share - % - Year The company announced earnings of $3.89 per share, up 15.7% year over year, beating expectations of $3.83, on revenue of $88.3 billion, up 12.6% from the previous year, higher than the expected $87.1 billion.Apple's strong growth in services, revenues from other devices, and its capital return to investors signal that the company can look past a weaker quarter of iPhone sales — which is still seen as Apple's most prominent driver of revenue growth — and still deliver profits. Belief - Wall - Street - IPhone - X The initial belief around Wall Street was that the iPhone X would draw first-time users and people looking to upgrade their phones, but Apple's December quarter earnings results showed that was not the case, Oppenheimer analyst Andrew Uerkwitz said.Apple's stock price slipped 2.74% to $163.19 a share on the Friday morning after earnings. Uerkwitz - IPhone - Price - Tag - Consumers Uerkwitz believes the iPhone's higher price tag will be "harder to justify," leading consumers to delay upgrading their phones. Apple said that its iPhones had a higher average selling price (ASP) of nearly $800 this quarter, or $100 higher than last year due to the higher-priced iPhone X, which sells at $999.While the higher price may have helped revenue growth, Apple CEO Tim Cook parried questions about how many people were switching from Android phones to iPhones during an earnings call, a figure that it usually discloses.
